steps.name: Sample structure QC and covariate balance
caveats: The QC must be blind to the design so it cannot pre-shape the model fit
steps.context: Data: /eval-four-models-v2-with-covariates-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples + index column, gene-level counts from Salmon as delivered) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-covariates-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows; columns condition, sex, age). 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. Sex is F/M, age in years.
steps.question: Do the 12 adipose samples group by treatment, is any sample an outlier, and how balanced are sex and age between treated and control before the model is fitted?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf; plus a covariate-balance check because the design holds sex and age

steps.description: Blind variance-stabilizing QC of the 12 adipose samples plus a balance check of the sex and age covariates across treated and control, and a record of what the gene identifiers in counts.csv actually are.
acceptance_criteria: PCA and sample-distance heatmap computed on blind vst of the filtered counts, colored by condition, sex, and age
Report states whether samples separate by condition and whether any sample departs from its group
Sex-by-condition and age-by-condition balance table produced; near-confounding (e.g. all samples of one sex in one group, or age ranges barely overlapping) explicitly flagged in the step output
Gene identifier type of counts.csv (symbol vs Ensembl etc.) confirmed and recorded

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with sex and age in the design
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
With 6 replicates per cell, DESeq2 flags a gene with a count outlier by Cook's distance and sets its p-value to NA rather than replacing the count (R-0039); report those genes separately
Do not scale, transform, or pre-normalize the counts (R-0026)
steps.context: Input: filtered counts and metadata from T1S1. Design ~ sex + age + condition; contrast condition treated vs control. With 12 samples and 4 coefficients the residual df is 8, so power is limited and results are reported as such.
steps.question: Which genes differ between treated and control adipose samples after holding sex and age fixed in the model (~ sex + age + condition)?

grounding.reason: Raw counts, 6 per group, covariates sex and age: DESeq2 Wald with apeglm shrinkage per R-0001@9a17; covariates enter as design terms per R-0023@e919; length offset absent per R-0169@18ab

steps.description: Fit ~ sex + age + condition in DESeq2 on the 12x12,000 count matrix, test treated vs control with the Wald test, shrink the reported log2 fold change with apeglm, and apply BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering.
acceptance_criteria: deseq2 results table written with gene id, baseMean, log2FoldChange (unshrunken), lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, and shrunken log2FoldChange (apeglm) with the shrinkage estimator named in the header
Explicit reference level and named contrast condition=treated/control documented; positive log2FC means higher in treated
p-value histogram inspected and its shape reported before trusting padj
Number of genes tested after pre-filter, number of DE genes at padj < 0.05, and number with NA padj from outlier flagging vs independent filtering all reported
Model summary for the sex and age terms retained (covariate effects and whether age is estimable given the group imbalance)

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness check
caveats: Do not present the union of the two methods as the result; the intersection is the high-confidence set and disagreement is expected to grow at low counts (R-0042)
steps.context: Input: same filtered counts as T1S2. edgeR quasi-likelihood is the stated alternative for robustness at 2-11 replicates per group (M-0003, R-0001@9a17).
steps.question: Do the DESeq2 treated-vs-control calls hold under a second count model (edgeR QL F-test) on the same design?

grounding.reason: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test is the permitted second method at 2-11 replicates per group per R-0001@9a17; the two-method overlap is reported per R-0042@54e1

constraints: Use TMM normalization inside edgeR; no pre-normalized counts
steps.description: Refit the identical design (~ sex + age + condition, age centered) with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as a second method, and compute the overlap with the DESeq2 calls.
acceptance_criteria: edgeR QL F-test results table written for the same contrast with the same design terms
Overlap table of DESeq2 and edgeR significant gene sets produced: intersection size, DESeq2-only, edgeR-only
Intersection gene set written out as the high-confidence set, single-method genes labeled with their method

steps.name: Differential expression report
caveats: With 12 samples and residual df 8 the power is limited; treat single-method and low-count calls as preliminary, and interpret the covariate-adjusted effect with the group age imbalance in view
steps.context: Inputs: DESeq2 results from T1S2 and edgeR results from T2S1. A human UniProt ID-mapping table (UniProtKB -> gene symbol/Entrez) is available in the reference store should the gene identifiers need mapping to symbols.
steps.question: What is the final, reproducible answer to which genes differ between treated and control after adjustment for sex and age, and how confident are the calls?

grounding.reason: No rule covers this step as a whole; its constraints follow the reporting rules R-0085@bb37, R-0087@3dcc, R-0041@059a, R-0086@becf

constraints: report: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124)
steps.description: Assemble the final treated-vs-control DE report: full gene table with both fold-change estimates, fit diagnostics, the DESeq2-edgeR overlap, the covariate-adjustment statement, and the reproducibility record.
acceptance_criteria: Report contains: method and package versions, design formula and named contrast, thresholds, n_tested, per-group DE counts, MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram
Gene table carries unshrunken log2FC, shrunken log2FC (apeglm, named in header), lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value; p-values from the unshrunken fit
Overlap of DESeq2 and edgeR calls reported with the intersection as the high-confidence set
Report states that counts are used without a length offset (Salmon gene table, no quant.sf / avg-length input) and that isoform-use changes can appear as DE
Reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, seed

If counts.csv gene identifiers are not HGNC symbols, a symbol column is added via the human UniProt ID-mapping reference; if that reference cannot resolve the identifier space, the table ships with the delivered identifiers and the gap is stated rather than guessed

plan.title: Treated vs control adipose DE adjusted for sex and age
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is which genes differ between the 6 treated and 6 control adipose samples when subjects also differ in sex and age and the groups are not age-matched. Sex and age therefore enter the model as fixed-effect design terms beside condition (per rule R-0023): the design is ~ sex + age + condition, with age centered before the fit because it is continuous. Normalization stays inside the model as DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors; counts are used as delivered (Salmon gene-level table with no per-sample quantification files or average-transcript-length table available, so the length offset is lost and an isoform-use change can appear as DE - stated in the report, per R-0169). The pre-filter is minimal (10 counts in the smallest group) with DESeq2 independent filtering doing the rest; BH at alpha 0.05 with the p-value histogram inspected before adjustment. Because 6 replicates per group sits at the low end where DE tools disagree, the same design is also fitted with edgeR quasi-likelihood, and the report presents the intersection as the high-confidence set (R-0042). A blind-vst QC precedes the fits to check that samples group by condition and that no sample departs from its group, plus a covariate-balance check since age is not matched across groups. 12 samples x 12,000 genes is small, so resource needs are modest.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind variance stabilizing transform with PCA and sample distance heatmap
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (robustness check, same design)
DE analysis report with MA and dispersion plots and method overlap

parameters.value: method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info

steps.method: DESeq2 blind variance stabilizing transform with PCA and sample distance heatmap
Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (robustness check, same design)
DE analysis report with MA and dispersion plots and method overlap

plan.title: Treated vs control adipose DE adjusted for sex and age
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is which genes differ between the 6 treated and 6 control adipose samples when subjects also differ in sex and age and the groups are not age-matched. Sex and age therefore enter the model as fixed-effect design terms beside condition (per rule R-0023): the design is ~ sex + age + condition, with age centered before the fit because it is continuous. Normalization stays inside the model as DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors; counts are used as delivered (Salmon gene-level table with no per-sample quantification files or average-transcript-length table available, so the length offset is lost and an isoform-use change can appear as DE - stated in the report, per R-0169). The pre-filter is minimal (10 counts in the smallest group) with DESeq2 independent filtering doing the rest; BH at alpha 0.05 with the p-value histogram inspected before adjustment. Because 6 replicates per group sits at the low end where DE tools disagree, the same design is also fitted with edgeR quasi-likelihood, and the report presents the intersection as the high-confidence set (R-0042). A blind-vst QC precedes the fits to check that samples group by condition and that no sample departs from its group, plus a covariate-balance check since age is not matched across groups. 12 samples x 12,000 genes is small, so resource needs are modest.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
